Select sprite 7 and sample the right-side offset; terrain $5B-$62 requires the shared Y-alignment test.
Recognize ladder-side glyphs $65/$67 and nudge X two pixels toward their center, returning zero when a correction occurs. The narrow rope uses $63 with anchor $64; ladder center is $66.
Return carry from the low three X bits: carry clear means the player X is aligned to an eight-pixel tile boundary.
Shared entry accepting X coordinate in A. Three right shifts test its lowest three bits; carry is clear only when all three were zero.
For ladder-center glyph $66, snap X to the next/previous eight-pixel alignment according to bits 1-2, maintaining the VIC X-high bit on overflow.
Alternate centering entry skips the glyph test. Use X bits 1-2 to move to an eight-pixel boundary and update VIC X-high on carry.
Reject a left jump into blocking terrain; otherwise select the left jumping pose, set the negative horizontal flag and enter the running-jump setup.
Reject a right jump against the complementary slopes/walls; otherwise choose the right jumping pose and positive running-jump direction.
Permit standing jump on solid/rope terrain except the forbidden supporting configurations; select the vertical jump sequence.
On a new cast press, refuse if HUD charge digit is zero; otherwise decrement it, set pending-cast flag $C02D=$FF, and show the facing-specific casting pose.
Set death flag $C02A=1 and clear active jump and forced tile-effect state. Caller returns to the compiled game flow to process the death.
Preserve the selected pose and carry direction, take two horizontal steps and four downward pixels, play sliding sound and apply the pose.

Nineteen packed bytes, traversed backwards after initializing remaining=19; indices 18..1 execute and index 0 is the terminating step. Bit 0 requests a two-pixel horizontal move, bits 5/6 each request one vertical pixel, bit 7 selects upward. Clear-space standing and running arcs reach thirteen pixels above takeoff. Terrain can end either early.
Nineteen packed steps for a horizontal jump, selected at $76D1. The jump loop uses direction flags in $C094 and checks terrain/collisions between steps.
Set the jump step pointer to vertical_jump_steps, then enter common jump initialization.
Point to running_jump_steps. Common initialization debounces held FIRE, cancels forced tile motion, starts 19 jump ticks and configures SID voice 3.

Continue packed jump, but matching lower-left/right rope $63, anchor $64 or ladder-center $66 probes end it immediately. Platform/anchor and slope tests can end it before the countdown expires. Prepared replay records include clear jumps, rope and ladder catches; player outputs were compared live.
Sixteen low and sixteen high frequency bytes for jump sound on SID voice 3. Indexed by remaining jump count minus three.
High-byte halves of the sixteen jump-sound frequencies. Sixteen low and sixteen high frequency bytes for jump sound on SID voice 3. Indexed by remaining jump count minus three.
Use cached tile $C02F and sprite 7 coordinate offset; the shared entry at $7823 also handles other sprites. Compute slope height from X low bits and write corrected Y, returning carry set on a slope.

Shared slope-height entry: X is the VIC coordinate-pair offset, $8F the terrain glyph. Derive horizontal phase and tile-row baseline, then write slope-corrected sprite Y and return carry set when a slope was recognized.
A is the first sprite shape; save it at $C367 and select zero animation span before shared update.
Save pose A and request animation span two; shared code updates sprite 7 and facing arrow in the HUD.
Save pose A and select three-frame oscillating animation.
Save pose A and select four-frame oscillating animation before rendering the player and direction indicator.
X is actor slot. Reset frame/direction when the base shape changes, optionally mirror the image for facing, store the current sprite pointer and ping-pong frame offset within its span.
RTS ending actor animation update, also used as a one-byte-before base for four direction glyph reads. The glyph table begins at $7912.
Four screen glyphs $6E-$71 for right/left/up/down, read with direction 1-4 using base $7911 (the preceding RTS byte is not a fifth arrow).
Test player Y minus $25 against mask 6; the alternate entry $791A uses mask 7 for full eight-pixel alignment. Carry clear means aligned.
Select mask 7 instead of the normal mask 6, subtract the sprite-to-tile Y origin $25 and report unaligned with carry set.
Carry clear moves sprite 7 right two pixels; carry set moves left two. Update D010 bit 7 when low X wraps.
Direct bytecode-callable entries select effects 6,4,1 at $794E/$7952/$7956, then share the state/color/sound setup with tile effects.
Map glyphs $6C-$71 to six effects. Question-mark glyph $3F chooses an effect from random state with zero giving none and seven mapping to one; switch player to hires and play a sound.
If $C035 is nonzero, clear death state, patch a relative branch through tile_effect_branches and jump to teleport/death/right/up/left/down effect handling.
Relative branch operand patched by effect number through $79AC. The following JMP slots dispatch teleport, death and four forced directions.
Tile-effect dispatch slot 1: JMP selected through the patched branch at $7998. Effects are teleport, death, right, up, left and down in slot order.
Tile-effect dispatch slot 2: JMP selected through the patched branch at $7998. Effects are teleport, death, right, up, left and down in slot order.
Tile-effect dispatch slot 3: JMP selected through the patched branch at $7998. Effects are teleport, death, right, up, left and down in slot order.
Tile-effect dispatch slot 4: JMP selected through the patched branch at $7998. Effects are teleport, death, right, up, left and down in slot order.
Tile-effect dispatch slot 5: JMP selected through the patched branch at $7998. Effects are teleport, death, right, up, left and down in slot order.
Tile-effect dispatch slot 6: JMP selected through the patched branch at $7998. Effects are teleport, death, right, up, left and down in slot order.
Seven branch offsets 0,0,3,6,9,12,15. Effect 1-6 patches the BPL at $7998 to one of six JMPs, dispatching teleport, death or forced directional travel.
Exchange player coordinates and X-high state with the saved teleport location; first use chooses the level start. Add a random horizontal nudge and restore ordinary movement.
Cancel the visual effect, discard this helper return address and transfer to the player-death flag setter.
Move player right four pixels and sample the forward tile; continue forced motion only while its allowed terrain test holds.
Leftward four-pixel version of the forced-motion effect, sharing the blocking-tile resolver.
Move up two pixels and sample feet; stop the effect on a platform/slope at the required alignment, otherwise return through the forced-motion continuation.
Move down two pixels and share the vertical effect termination tests.
Restore sprite 7 multicolor, sound the transition and clear the shared transient player state through $8F79.
Skip protected climbing/jumping situations, otherwise kill on unsupported blank/off-platform tiles or on hazard glyphs $72-$75 with a sprite-background collision.

Glyph $40 exits only after key flag $C030 is set; store exit position, animate disappearance and set $C02C=$80. Glyphs $1B-$1F are removed on contact: $1B is the key and replenishes charges from the level header; others go to treasure scoring. Live forced-tile check: key at the sampled cell sets key flag and restores charge digit3; matching control has neither change.
Count down the sprite-6 reward display and vary its color; the main player update removes it near expiry.
Cycle colors over up to sixteen recorded treasure cells and sixteen hazards. Every second interrupt update cycle the hazard screen glyph through $72-$75.
Three colors cycled over the recorded treasure/object cells by $7B27.
Three colors for the recorded animated hazard cells, paired with the four-frame glyph animation at $7B6D.
Scan playable screen backwards, retaining at most sixteen treasure/object locations ($1C-$1F) and sixteen hazard locations ($72-$75). Fill unused slots with the harmless bottom-right offset $3F7.
Test ($FB),Y for $1C-$1F, record its low offset and screen-page number, then decrement Y. Exhausting the sixteen slots unwinds to the hazard scan.
Record glyphs $72-$75 into the hazard offset arrays; once sixteen entries are found, unwind the scanner and return.
Disable game interrupts, install IRQ epilogue $7D6A and NMI RTI $7D6F, select bank $37 and copy the visible ROM NMI vector into underlying RAM at $FFFA/B.
Disable game sources, restore KERNAL vectors/messages and enable CIA1 timer A interrupts before returning with interrupts enabled.
Install $7CBF, enable VIC sprite-sprite collision IRQ bit 2, load CIA1 timer B with $FFFF and enable its interrupt/start bit. Read both collision latches, then CLI.
Stop CIA1 timer B and CIA2 timers, mask VIC and CIA interrupt sources, and acknowledge pending VIC flags. Does not itself change the CPU interrupt-disable flag.

VIC collision IRQ dispatches through D01E; otherwise acknowledge CIA1 and update cell animation, random state, bonus timer, dissolve, popup fade, flashing terrain and pause keys. Return via the KERNAL-compatible register epilogue.

Read the sprite collision latch. Player collisions ignore sprite 6, matching exempt color and type 20; type 7 can become a supporting elevator. Without player bit 7, select the two highest set sprite bits. An active sprite-6 projectile queues the other slot without testing actor type or color; cat/type 20 versus rat/type 14 queues the rat with bit 7 set. Original-code tests cover all actor slots/types for spells 0-4 and every cat/rat slot pair. Forced latches test dispatch, not collision geometry.

After a sprite-collision latch selected elevator slot Y, compute ADC #14 then SBC elevatorY WITHOUT SEC. For ordinary player Y<242 the ADC carry is clear, so accept (playerY+13-elevatorY) modulo 256 in 0..2. Set $C02B=2 and supporting slot $C033. All six slots and eight nearby height offsets checked against the original IRQ; collision geometry is separate.
An active projectile queues target slot+1 in $C039. This path has no actor-type or color immunity test; player-present collisions were handled above.

Test the two selected actors for a type 20 cat and type 14 rat, in either slot order. Queue the rat index OR $80. The mainline handles that signed queue before examining the selected spell, so even Freeze does not protect a rat from the cat.
Pop Y, X and A saved by the KERNAL IRQ prologue and RTI. The final RTI at $7D6F is also the installed NMI handler.
Decrement the shared animation/freeze phase and call the actor controller for slots 5 through 0, preserving each slot index around the call.

FB identifies an actor or projectile. Enforce type-dependent screen bounds, reset/turn expired actors, apply signed X/Y velocities including X-high-bit carry, and resolve terrain/ladder support before rendering animation.
For ground-following actors clear support flags, inspect rope and foot tiles, fall up to seven pixels when unsupported, reverse on edges, align to platforms/slopes and record ladder availability.
Use actor type to choose an animation mask/facing; type 19 first tries to eat a treasure. Projectile slot 6 skips the actor-type table. Pass the final mirror selector to animate_actor_sprite.
Test actor Y minus $25 for eight-pixel alignment using carry through three shifts. X is the doubled sprite index.
Type 19 samples its center tile, removes $1C-$1F treasure, plays reward sound, runs the linked terrain change and level callback, then animates with mask one.
21 masks indexed by actor type. Zero updates every movement call; nonzero permits animation only when mask AND the shared phase $C0A2 is zero. Type 19 instead runs the treasure-eating path.
Restore six eight-byte character images from copies $0400 bytes above their font destinations, undoing per-level graphic alterations.
Six little-endian font destinations: $C8E8,$CAD8,$CAE0,$CB18,$CB20,$CB28. $7FC0 restores each from the corresponding address plus $0400.
PP&S marker then zero fill between the glyph restore table and the next code page; no dispatch table in the engine names this interval.
Nine-byte cartridge-style header: cold-start vector $8009, warm-start word $3133 and CBM80 signature. A reset seeing this RAM signature can enter the resident border-color trap at $8009.
Install the harmless NMI RTI, disable interrupts and repeatedly increment border/background colors. No ordinary game caller to this diagnostic entry has been established.
Normally RTS. Demo initialization replaces it with NOP so execution falls into the recorded-input player at $801E; live recording is the alternate signed branch at $8051.

Replay joystick bytes through the CIA port with run lengths from ($AC),Y, advancing $C03A when the count expires. Actual FIRE exits to the program menu. The alternate branch records changed input and increments its run length.
Load the selected input run length through ($AC),Y into $C03B and return. The following record-mode branch compares live CIA input, extending a matching run or storing a new input/run-length pair.
Clear demo selection/index, point value/count streams at $5200/$5280, enable the input hook and fill the 256-byte buffer with ones, ending with neutral joystick $1F.
Clear screen colors, enable the input hook, force speed 7, select input and level pages by demo number, copy the level image and run ordinary level setup.
Three pages $9A,$99,$58 holding recorded joystick values at offset zero and run lengths at offset $80. $80A2 selects them by demo number minus one.
Three source pages $9B,$5E,$59. $8E79 copies $470 bytes from the selected page into $C300-$C76F for attract-mode play.
Clear demo selection, restore RTS at the input hook and set default game speed 5.
Configure SID voice 3 with zero sustain/release and a noise waveform; player X low bits vary pitch and gate. Reset sliding-pitch counter $B2 to 100.
On alternating Y pixels gate voice 3; on the other pixels fold height into a note/octave and convert through $8437, producing position-dependent climbing tones.
Configure filtered noise on voice 3 and toggle its gate with player Y parity, producing the rope/ladder friction effect.
Decrease the pitch counter by three, wrapping to 100 on negative, and retrigger voice 3 triangle on a sliding step.
Initialize all three voice envelopes and fixed frequency components for the first terrain-drawing pass.
Every eight construction steps retrigger three voices, delay, then resume the screen-cell scan at $924F.
Set two pulse voice envelopes/widths and starting note $2F for the rope/end glyph construction pass.
Every eight cells advance a valid semitone, convert its frequency and apply it to two detuned pulse voices, then resume the renderer.
Start sustained triangle/ring-modulated voices and an ascending frequency accumulator for ladder drawing.
Add $0040 to the construction pitch, write voice 1 frequency, delay nine units and continue the screen scan.
Configure pulse/triangle voices, zero the note index and set envelopes for multi-character object construction.
Only on the first glyph $68 of each object, play the next scale note on voice 1 and a quarter-frequency voice 3, with a noise/ring voice 2 layer. Delay, then resume cell scanning.
Two eleven-note sequences for terrain construction sounds; $82F7 uses the first and $836A uses the second via base $8352.

Second eleven-note construction sequence, selected by the alternate sound entry. Two eleven-note sequences for terrain construction sounds; $82F7 uses the first and $836A uses the second via base $8352.
Silence voice 3, reset note index and set voice 2 low frequency for the arrow/effect-tile construction pass.
Play the next note from the second construction scale on voice 1, retrigger voice 2 and delay before resuming the screen scan.
Play fixed three-voice chord/noise combination for a key tile, delay 180 units and rejoin the terrain renderer.
Play a second fixed three-voice chord for the exit glyph, wait 255 delay units and continue rendering.
Skip invalid low-nibble semitone values $C and $F by adding/subtracting four in $B1; other note encodings return unchanged.
Convert packed octave/semitone $B1 to 16-bit frequency $AE/$AF using twelve low-byte bases with implicit high byte 1 and octave shifts.
Twelve frequency low bytes with implicit high byte 1. $8437 shifts that 16-bit value left by the octave encoded in $B1 bits 4-6.

A is treasure class 1-4; add difficulty, show its points sprite if no projectile is active, remove/update linked terrain and invoke the level callback. Add the selected decimal digits into the seven-character HUD score and test the extra-life threshold. Live: first treasure adds50; starting9950 yields10000 and lives6 to7. Original-code tests cover all16 treasure/difficulty combinations at five score boundaries.

Seven tens-column additions 5,0,0,0,0,0,5, paired with the hundreds-column table at $84DF. Treasure class plus difficulty selects 50,100,200,300,400,500,750 points; the eight-digit HUD keeps its final zero unchanged.

Hundreds-column additions 0,1,2,3,4,5,7. The preceding table supplies the tens digit; the HUD has a trailing zero. Seven unit-digit and seven tens-digit additions for treasure class plus difficulty. $8464 inserts them into a seven-digit decimal addition buffer, then adds into HUD score.
Copy player X/Y into sprite 6 and copy X-high bit 7 into bit 6 while preserving other bits; enable sprite 6.
If HUD score digit at $C7BA changed during addition, increment $C008 and draw a life icon when fewer than ten icons are already shown.
Zero seven bytes $92-$98 used as the digit-wise score addition buffer.
Reset and retrigger SID voices 1/2 with fixed frequencies and triangle/ring waveforms for collecting treasure.

Decrement contact lifetime $C02B, select slot $C033. With jump remaining below 14 set wizard Y=elevatorY-13 and feet=$5C; during the first jump steps add its Y velocity instead. This routine does not add elevator X velocity. Continue at $7174. Vertical ride outputs compared with live execution.
Select pixel offsets 25 horizontally and 29 vertically, then read the screen tile for sprite index FB.
Select horizontal offset zero and vertical offset 29; the common sampler returns the tile at the sprite right side.
Use offsets 16 and 35 to inspect the lower-left support/collectible tile around an actor.
Use offsets 9 and 35 to inspect the lower-right support/collectible tile.
Use offsets 12 and 30 to sample the sprite center row used for pickups and alignment checks.
Use offsets 12 and 29 for the foot/terrain sample. Shared code computes row*40+$C400 and column from nine-bit X, returns screen byte and pointer/index, and normalizes $F3 to solid $5C.
Sprite bit masks placed at even indices 0,2,...14 so the same X index can address VIC coordinate pairs and the X-high-bit mask.

Final even-indexed mask $80 for sprite 7, after the seven actor/effect masks. Sprite bit masks placed at even indices 0,2,...14 so the same X index can address VIC coordinate pairs and the X-high-bit mask.

FB selects one of six actors. Apply type-specific update divisors, thaw color 3 on phase expiry, activate its sprite if needed, and dispatch type 1-13 to special motion; higher types follow terrain and sometimes pursue player axes.

Ground/ladder controller shared by types 14-20, including the cat. Choose motion using terrain flags, SID randomness and distance to the wizard's coordinates through $8766/$89D9/$8A02; there is no separate rat target search on this path. Type-specific incidental sounds follow; cat/rat removal is in the collision handler.
Return nonzero except when shared animation phase is divisible by eight and random state bit 0 is zero; actor controllers use this to throttle incidental sounds.
Compare coarse horizontal and vertical distance from the actor to player using nine-bit X positions; carry chooses which pursuit axis to favor.
Set vertical velocity toward the player, then restrict it according to ladder/support flags; return zero velocity when vertical travel is unavailable.
Type 1 waits for its cooldown/random trigger, spawns near player Y from the opposite horizontal edge, selects one of two directional shapes and moves at three pixels per update.
Clear this actor bit in D01B so the activated sprite appears in front of character graphics.
Play the pulse effect at $985A, then enter ordinary movement for the current actor.
Types 2,3,5 choose X/Y velocity toward the player and a random movement duration shortened by difficulty*8; sometimes suppress Y motion. Type 2 also triggers its buzzing sound.
Type 4 independently chooses each pursuit axis when a random byte is at least 150, then moves for 1-8 ticks.
Type 13 sets its movement duration to 255 then enters the shared actor movement/terrain routine.
Type 6 waits its cooldown, chooses an X offset near the player, spawns at Y=$20 with downward velocity two and a 90-tick run, and computes the next cooldown using the signed random offset.
Type 7 starts with signed X/Y velocity nibbles from level field $C316+slot, or negates both velocities on the next leg. Leg duration comes from $C35F.
Negate signed X and Y velocities for actor Y; used by elevators and terrain-following turns.
Types 8-10 have zero velocity and a 255-tick movement duration; the shared animation still runs.
Restore color and starting position from the level header, put blank shape $E4 in its pointer and enable the actor bit in D015.
Type 11 alternates vertical velocity -1/+1 every twenty movement ticks, holds X still, and sounds at the upward transition.
Type 12 alternates vertical velocity -1/+1 every ten movement ticks; the top-level dispatcher also divides its update rate by four.
Compare full nine-bit actor X against player X and choose signed horizontal speed from $C06E/$C06F.
Compare actor Y with player Y and store velocity +1, zero or -1 toward the player.
Clear the actor type, save its slot in FB and start a sprite-dissolve disappearance.
Load CHRW into $C800 and SPRW into $E000 through KERNAL LOAD using device 8; return the final disk status in FB.
PETSCII CHRW and SPRW names used by $8A22 to reload the charset at $C800 and sprites at $E000.

Disable sprites, build LnnT filename from FB and load the level at its stored address. On status $40 run state initialization, speed-key check, colored terrain construction, bottom border, cell indexing and spell-name rendering; return disk status in FB.
Seven-byte DOS scratch command: S0: followed by mutable LnnT at $8AB7-$8ABA. KERNAL SETNAM supplies the length; there is no string terminator in this record.
PETSCII L starts the four-byte filename LnnT. Terrain drawing temporarily reuses $8AB7/$8AB8 as its indirect sound callback; $8BBD reconstructs the filename before disk access.
Mutable tens digit of the level number. Also the high byte of the temporary terrain-drawing sound callback; $8BBD restores it before disk access.
Mutable units digit of the LnnT filename, produced by repeated subtraction at $8BBD.
PETSCII T ends the four-byte LnnT name; KERNAL receives its explicit length, with no zero terminator.

Protect the supplied game disk: $8B98 LOADs PPSS and leaves Z set when status is $40 (marker read succeeded). That case returns FB=1 without saving. Otherwise construct LnnT, initialize/scratch the destination and SAVE $C300-$C76F. Live: private original-disk copy rejected; blank private disk saved L99T with status 0 and reloaded identical reset elevator fields.
Load SCOR into $C100 with device 8 secondary address zero and return disk status in FB.
Initialize the disk, scratch SCOR, disable KERNAL messages and SAVE exactly $C100-$C17F. Return the final disk status in FB.
I0 disk-initialize command, S0: scratch prefix, and SCOR filename. The score saver scratches and writes exactly $80 bytes from $C100.
Clear open-file count, OPEN command I0 on logical/device/secondary 15/8/15 and close it again.
X/Y point to seven-byte command S0: plus filename. Send it with OPEN 15,8,15 and CLOSE 15.

Try to LOAD marker file PPSS at $0340, then compare READST with $40. Equality identifies the protected original game disk, so the caller REFUSES its save. The marker is not a prerequisite for writing a custom disk.
PETSCII PPSS; $8B98 loads this marker file at $0340 and returns whether disk status equals $40 before allowing a level save.
Convert level number FB to two decimal digits by repeated subtraction of ten, write LnnT into $8AB7-$8ABA. No range guard is present in this helper.

Complete an expired dissolve, manage popup cleanup, consume $C039 hit queue, handle cast requests, and move an active projectile. Negative queued indices remove the cat-contact rat directly. Positive queues skip hits during $C066 transient state, otherwise spell 4 freezes and spells 0-3 all remove the target. Original-code matrix: 7,200 cases across five spells, 20 types,six slots,three colors,four difficulties; five forced queued hits and no-hit control also checked live. Cast IDs 0-4 launch sprite 6 with direction-table velocity; higher IDs send an event to bytecode through $C02C.
The queued projectile hit tests only whether spell ID is 4. IDs0-3 take the same actor-removal call at $8C16, consistent with the supplied manual. Sprite shape/color are separate level fields.

Freeze sets victim color 3 and resets shared phase $C0A2 to 109-16*difficulty for difficulty 0-3:109, 93, 77, 61 actor-update passes. All frozen actors use this one phase. A later hit resets it for earlier victims too. Controller $862E waits for zero, then restores each saved color.
Overlapping four-entry X and Y step tables: X={5,-5,0,0}; Y={0,0,-3,3}. Selected by facing minus one when casting a projectile spell.

Four signed vertical steps 0,0,-3,+3, overlapping the last two horizontal zeroes. Overlapping four-entry X and Y step tables: X={5,-5,0,0}; Y={0,0,-3,3}. Selected by facing minus one when casting a projectile spell.
Start player sprite dissolve, then sweep voice-2 frequency over fourteen rising ramps with short delays.

FB is sprite pointer and FC desired facing marker. Bank all RAM in, reverse the order of two-bit pixels in each byte and swap outside bytes of each row when the stored marker differs, then restore bank $37 and interrupts.
Fifteen loaded values between the sprite mirror and spell-name renderer. No traced engine operand names them; their original use is not established.

Draw the selected 13-character spell name. Address construction clears carry for every valid spell ID 0-11; both player and thief call this immediately before the level callback. Consequently the ADC in L21T receives carry clear and assigns type 2+(treasure_index&3). Checked across twelve IDs, sixteen indices and both earlier carry inputs.
Twelve byte offsets 0,13,...143 into spell_names. $8D4B adds the selected offset to $8D73 and copies thirteen characters into the HUD.

Twelve fixed-width spell labels, 13 screen-code bytes each: FIREBALL, MAGIC MISSILE, DISINTEGRATE, ENCHANTMENT, FREEZE, INVISIBILITY, TELEPORT, FEATHER FALL, LEVITATE, HASTE, SLOW and NONE. Uppercase glyphs use $41-$5A directly; spaces pad the status display field.
Move previous random byte to $C032; subtract CIA timer-A low from SID oscillator output into $C031. Derive a signed magnitude 0-7 from a second oscillator read into $C06D.
Clear color RAM $D800-$DB47, covering the playfield while leaving the lower HUD area outside this loop.
Wait twice with A=$FF using the register-preserving delay routine after a disk save.
Load delay count from FB and fall through to the common busy wait; alternate entry $8E58 accepts A directly and preserves X/Y.
Busy-wait entry with delay in A. Preserve X/Y, decrement a nested Y counter and X delay count, then restore both registers. Zero A wraps through 256 X iterations.
Fill $C770-$C7E7 with spaces, preserving the sprite pointer table.
FB is the source high page. Copy $470 bytes backwards from that source into $C300-$C76F, including actor header, callback/patch records and screen cells.

Clear transient state and SID registers, initialize VIC sprite mode, movement speeds, bonus bar and timer, sprite bit masks and timed-terrain counters from the level header. Restore six mutable character images.
Clear six actor sprites/velocities, give ground types starting X velocity/support handling, expand stationary types 8-10, configure keyboard/joystick ports, then clear transient player states.
Play the walking/reset sound and clear special-state, death, event, elevator-contact, tile-effect and jump flags plus SID filter routing.
Six cursor-bound fields for full-name entry, copied into $C067-$C06C by $8FC4. The shared editor uses start/end columns and current cursor coordinates.
Six cursor fields for the alternate bounded short-entry routine $8FB5; the game high-score script instead uses the third set at $8FA0.
Six cursor-bound fields {18,17,21,17,18,17} for the additional three-character input entry $8FA6.
Copy the third six-byte cursor setting to $C067-$C06C, choose timeout-enabled mode and enter the same bounded keyboard editor as initials/name entry.
Copy the alternate six-byte cursor bounds, select timeout-enabled mode and enter the shared keyboard editor. High-score initials use $8FA6, confirmed by SYS $7078 in bytecode $4541.

Copy full-name cursor bounds, blank the name line, disable timeout and enter the shared keyboard editor. Accept printable letters/digits/punctuation except quote, bounded by the end column; support delete and RETURN.
Advance flashing cursor character and decrement a coarse inactivity timer; in initials mode expiry unwinds to the editor return path. Full-name entry keeps waiting.
X is actor slot. Resolve its sprite pointer into VIC bank $C000, bank out ROM while retaining I/O, copy 64 bytes to $C2C0 and point that actor to workspace sprite $0B.
Scan KERNAL keyboard buffer once; ASCII digit 0-9 becomes game-speed byte $C005. Other keys leave speed unchanged.

Scan the playfield in passes for solid/sloped terrain, ropes, ladders, objects, effect arrows, key and exit. Use level header colors and patch an indirect sound callback per pass; FB=0 recolors silently, nonzero animates construction and checks speed keys.
Compare each screen glyph against base $92 and count $93. Matching cells get color $94; if animation enabled, jump through patched $8AB7 to the pass sound routine, which returns at $924F.
Set paired screen/color pointers $C700/$DB00 and Y=$6F to scan backward through $C400-$C76F.
Count $C095 down using level period $C350; on expiry decrement the 24-unit bonus $C034 and redraw a six-cell quarter-filled bar. Nonzero bonus retriggers a pitch proportional to time remaining.
Finish an earlier dissolve if present, copy sprite FB into the temporary buffer, encode its slot+1 in $C096 and start the disappearance sound.

Add sixteen to the dissolve counter per interrupt. Until wrap, clear selected pixel pairs in the 63-byte sprite image using SID noise, eight masks and bytes sampled from this code itself. On wrap set the completion flag.
Eight masks applied with SID noise while clearing pixels from the temporary sprite at $C2C0. The eight choices bias which multicolor pixel pairs disappear.
Extract actor slot from low nibble of $C096, disable its sprite bit and clear dissolve/completion state.
Place wizard and effect sprite at level start coordinates, initialize colors and pointers, sweep filtered noise, reveal the wizard, dissolve the effect sprite and finish by initializing actors.

Three level-defined timed runs switch glyphs between solid/absent, ladder/absent or slope/alternate forms. Timer reloads come from packed on/off durations; each run advances by its configured stride until a nonmatching glyph.

Find collected treasure in the sixteen-slot object index, then repeat its six-byte 3x2 replacement according to C320/C330 count and stride. Destinations are unrestricted: supplied patches write screen, color RAM, header state or VIC registers. Zero replacement bytes leave destinations alone. Player/thief callbacks execute after the patch, so regenerated treasure can drive repeated changes.
Add Y into FB/FC then subtract screen base high byte $C4, returning a zero-based screen offset for matching indexed objects.
Ignore collision death during special player state $C066; otherwise play type-6 or type-1 impact sounds where applicable and set death flag $C02A.

Enable player multicolor, choose initial bounce direction from joystick/terrain, follow the packed bounce sequence and animate four rotating shapes while falling. At the bottom run the final two-frame effect, read speed keys and silence the three voices.
